correctness.rationale: For every N>=n+1, coupling the focal payoff samples yields exact equation (1) and a degree-(n-1) polynomial in cooperator count. Under strictly increasing r with r(n)=n(N-1)/(N-n), the payoff difference has opposite strict signs at endpoints. A maximum of n-1 changes follows from real-root counting and for odd n parity reduces this to n-2. A rational sequence d_i and multipliers r(k)=n^2(1+S_k/k) at N=n+1 has positive strictly increasing multipliers, a strictly growing total benefit, and payoff gaps exactly d_i with the sharp sign pattern. The exact Fermi fixation ratio equals exp(beta sum_i d_i)=1. checker.py independently verified all n=2..20, 307 direct-vs-reduced rational payoffs, and 63 polynomial finite-difference identities; full quantifiers rely on written proof.

value.rationale: Group size bounds the complexity of local selective incentives in a finite multiplayer game. A complete parity-sharp bound under economically meaningful strict economies of scale and positive rising group benefits is nontrivial because prescribed oscillatory local fitness differences must coexist with the source paper’s terminal neutrality restriction. Explicit rational attaining witnesses for every n show that identical symmetric rare-mutation abundance cannot constrain the local selection landscape. This is a natural complete classification, not an arbitrary numerical slice; no empirical or global-outcome claim is made.
